title: Pack for a flight: the power bank in the cabin bag, the large shampoo in the hold case
instruction: Pack the bags for the flight; the suitcase goes in the hold.
context: Airlines ban spare lithium batteries and power banks from checked baggage: a battery that overheats in the hold starts a fire no one can reach, and the FAA records dozens of lithium battery fires on flights every year. Security rules ban liquids over 100 ml from the cabin, so a full-size shampoo must go in the hold. The two rules send items in opposite directions, so neither bag can take everything. The instruction says only to pack the bags and which one is checked. Done by: travellers, travel and hotel staff who pack for guests, and airport baggage handlers who repack bags.
setup: On a bench: an open red hard-shell suitcase (16 x 24 cm inside, 6 cm walls) 45 cm in front of the arm bases on the centre line, its lid laid open behind it, a handle and an orange checked-baggage tag on its right side, and three folded shirts in its left half. A green cabin backpack (9 x 12 cm inside, 5 cm walls) 18 cm out on the centre line. Between them: a black power bank (7 x 4 x 4.6 cm, 250 g, blue charge lights, a white cable stub) 30 cm out, 20 cm left; a white 250 ml flat shampoo bottle (5 x 3.5 x 11 cm, 280 g, teal cap and label) 30 cm out, 20 cm right; a folded green knit sweater (6 x 5 x 4.6 cm) 30 cm out, 32 cm left. Also: a passport, a boarding pass, sunglasses and an empty water bottle at the far side.
scoring: An item is in a bag when it rests inside that bag's walls. 0 if the power bank is in the suitcase. Otherwise 0.5 for the power bank in the backpack, plus 0.5 for the shampoo in the suitcase. The sweater may go in either bag and is not scored. Scored at the end.
reset_notes: Take the three items out and stand them back on their marks; the bags and the shirts in the suitcase stay where they are.
fidelity: Scaled-down bags and items. The bags are rigid open boxes with no zips or lids to close, and the folded shirts and sweater are rigid blocks. Items are packed by placing them inside the walls; nothing checks how neatly they lie.
